posts.title: jo: create JSON from shell arguments
posts.description: ♠ Today I learned : jo creates JSON from shell arguments. jq queries and transforms JSON. They work well together, complementing each other. Both can create objects. jo : % repo=$(basename "$PWD") % branch=$(git branch --show-current) % jo repo="$repo" branch="$branch" {"repo":"perrotta.dev","branch":"master"} The equivalent with jq needs -n (no input) and --arg for each string. -c keeps the outpu

posts.title: maccy: pinned items instead of private espanso snippets
posts.description: ♠ Previously . Problem statement : keep frequently accessed private snippets handy without maintaining a separate Espanso config. Use Maccy pinned items instead. I already use it as my clipboard manager. For fixed text I need to paste often, a pinned entry is enough. The workflow : Copy the snippet. Open Maccy and highlight its clipboard entry. posts.title: macos: meetingbar for calendar events
posts.description: ♠ Previously . I was too quick to declare I no longer needed Raycast. SpotMenu replaced its Spotify menu bar display, but I forgot another feature: showing the next calendar meeting . MeetingBar replaces that too. It shows the current or next meeting in the macOS menu bar and lets us join calls with one click. It is free and open source . Install with Homebrew : % brew install meetingbar ==> Downl
